results.evidence: Only the first ascensionist's own write-up states the 46 mi / 17,500 ft figure; the journal report gives no gain, and a third-party blog (a party met on the approach) only links to that same write-up. No independent second figure exists online for this twice-climbed route. Would be settled by a second party's trip report or a car-to-car GPS track stating total gain.

Re-checked: the journal report explicitly says the crux (short overhanging 5.9 choss) came on the second pitch, while the first ascensionist's pitch-by-pitch account (mirrored by pitch_detail, beta, obj_haz) puts the 5.9R crux on pitch 3. The two primary sources genuinely disagree (likely a different pitch count low on the route), so no number is adopted. Would be settled by a topo or a second party's pitch count.

results.fact: Approach time (approach prose 10-15 min vs timing.approachTimeHrs 0.12)
results.evidence: The Spire Gully area page and its Alpenkuhl sub-area page (same site, same guidebook-derived text) give a seven-minute approach from the hairpin; searches of other Washington Pass climbing pages (regional climbing overviews, the Hairpin Crags listings) found no independent approach time. One source only; would be settled by an independent trip report or the Mazama cragging guide's own figure.
